lines.trans: Wait—look at the faint blue lines drawn along the outer edges of each card!
Turn them face up on the flat bench slat like four tiles of one square...
Card One top left, Card Two top right, Card Three bottom left, Card Four bottom right!
Incredible! Together the four backs form a bird-eye drawing of Jasmine Courtyard!
There is our courtyard tree, there are the arched windows of Room Nine...
And look up on the second-floor wooden courtyard balcony—a bright red painted star!
Why did the mapmaker paint a red star on our upstairs courtyard balcony?!
Perhaps the small wax-sealed envelope in your pocket has the answer, Nour!
We walked every clue honestly—even Rami and his extra circle—so let us open it!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستنى, بيستنى).

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خطوط.

examples.trans: Your handwriting on the card is clear and neat.
Stay with me on the line a second.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: زرقا, plural: زرق).

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خفيفة, plural: خفاف).

examples.trans: Coffee with milk and light sugar.
A light, tasty breakfast in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مرسومة, plural: مرسومين).

examples.text: في مفتاح دهبي مرسوم فوق الباب.
examples.trans: There is a golden key painted above the door.
The map is drawn by hand.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: The word 'حافة' (el-Hawaaff) means 'the edges'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنوا—شوفوا الخطوط الزرقا الخفيفة المرسومة على الحواف الخارجية لكل كرت!
examples.trans: Wait—look at the faint blue lines drawn along the outer edges of each card!
This is حافة.

meanings.note: Describes outer shutters, doors, or walls facing the courtyard or street.

examples.text: رح ندهن الشيش الخارجي بلون أخضر دافي.
examples.trans: We are going to paint the outside shutters a warm green.

examples.text: الباب الخارجي بيفتح مباشرة على شارع الياسمين.
examples.trans: The exterior gate opens straight onto Jasmine Street.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كروت.

examples.text: بعتتله كرت بريد قصير الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: I sent him a short postcard last week.
I recognised his neat handwriting on the card right away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قلوب.

examples.trans: My heart is beating fast with joy!
Welcome from the bottom of my heart.

meanings.note: The word 'لفوق' (lafoq) means 'up'. It is a common adv in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اطنعشر دقة! أكيد هادا برج الساعة البلدي القديم تلات بلوكات لفوق!
examples.trans: Twelve chimes! That has to be the old municipal clock tower three blocks up!
This is لفوق.

meanings.note: Refers to a whiteboard (اللوح الأبيض), wooden plank, or windowpane (لوح قزاز).

examples.text: كتبنا مهام الأسبوع التلاتة عاللوح الأبيض.
examples.trans: We wrote the three tasks for the week on the whiteboard.

examples.text: نضفنا كل ألواح القزاز من الغبرة القديمة.
examples.trans: We cleaned all the glass panes of their old dust.

meanings.note: Noun of place from ق-ع-د ('to sit'); names the seat of a chair or a garden bench.

examples.text: ارفع مقعد الكرسي شوي عشان يطوي معك.
examples.trans: Lift the chair seat slightly so it folds for you.

examples.text: في مقعد خشب طويل تحت شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: There is a long wooden bench under the courtyard tree.

meanings.note: The word 'مسطح' (el-msaTTaH) means 'flat'. It is a common adj in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اقلبوهم لفوق على لوح المقعد المسطح زي أربع بلاطات لمربع واحد...
examples.trans: Turn them face up on the flat bench slat like four tiles of one square...
This is مسطح.

meanings.note: Spoken word for 'like': زيك 'like you'; زي ما 'just as, the way that'.

examples.trans: I want a glass of tea like yesterday.
Do it the way I taught you.

meanings.note: The word 'أربع' (arba3) means 'four'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اقلبوهم لفوق على لوح المقعد المسطح زي أربع بلاطات لمربع واحد...
examples.trans: Turn them face up on the flat bench slat like four tiles of one square...
This is أربع.

meanings.note: The word 'بلاطة' (blaaTaat) means 'tiles'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اقلبوهم لفوق على لوح المقعد المسطح زي أربع بلاطات لمربع واحد...
examples.trans: Turn them face up on the flat bench slat like four tiles of one square...
This is بلاطة.

meanings.note: Four-sided square pane of glass, tile, or ruled grid.

examples.text: أول مربع قزاز مسحناه بين السما الزرقا وراه.
examples.trans: The first glass square we wiped revealed the blue sky behind it.

examples.text: بلاط الساحة مقسم لمربعات حجر مرتبة.
examples.trans: The courtyard paving is laid out in neat stone squares.

meanings.note: Used both as the numeral 'one' and after a noun for emphasis ('a single, one and the same').

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('above, over') and standalone ('upstairs').

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: The word 'يسار' (yasaar) means 'left'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: يسار بعد قواوير الورد، ويسار كمان مرة بعد السور الأخضر—لوين رايحين؟!
examples.trans: Left past the flower pots, left again past the green fence—where are we going?!
This is يسار.

meanings.note: The word 'اتنين' (w-tnein) means 'and two'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: جمعوا الزوايا الأربعة مع بعض... ناوليني كرت واحد واتنين وتلاتة يا نور!
examples.trans: Bring all four corners together... hand me Cards One, Two, and Three, Nour!
This is اتنين.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The green pharmacy is on your right.
We hung the board to the right of the desk.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'three'; short form تلات (talaat) directly before a plural noun (تلات سنين 'three years').

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('under, beneath') and standalone ('downstairs').

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Numeral 'four'; short form أربع (arba') directly before a plural noun (أربع طاولات 'four tables').

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Negates nouns, adjectives, participles, and pronouns in spoken Jordanian (مش شنتتي 'not my bag', مش ملاقي 'cannot find').

examples.trans: This is not my suitcase!
Not bad for a second day at work!

meanings.note: Standalone معقول! is a classic Jordanian exclamation of amazed disbelief ('No way! / Could it really be?!').

examples.text: معقول! قطار جدي الخشب لسا موجود!
examples.trans: Could it be! Grandfather's wooden train is still around!
The price is reasonable and fair for everyone.

meanings.note: Pronounced duhur in everyday Jordanian: الظهر means 'at noon / midday'.

examples.trans: He will arrive Friday at noon.
The sun is high at midday.

meanings.note: After a plural verb, بعض means 'each other' (بننادي بعض 'we call each other').

examples.trans: We call each other by first name here.

examples.text: ما حكينا مع بعض من زمان.
examples.trans: We have not spoken with each other in a long time.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعمل, بيعمل).

examples.text: اليوم رح نعمل بيض عالطريقة الفرنسية!
examples.trans: Today we will make French-style eggs!
What do we do now with the rain coming down?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: رسمات.

examples.text: في رسمة مفتاح دهبي فوق الباب.
examples.trans: There is a drawing of a golden key above the door.
His pencil sketches are very detailed.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: The word 'لـ' (لـ) means 'لـ'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: معها حق—أنا عم أعمل لفائف القرفة لفترة بعد الظهر لـ بيت الياسمين.
examples.trans: She is right—I am making the afternoon cinnamon rolls for Jasmine Courtyard.
This is لـ.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: The word 'الياسمين' (الياسمين) means 'الياسمين'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شو هالصباح الحلو يوم السبت لمشية كنز بشارع شارع الياسمين!
examples.trans: What a glorious Saturday morning for a treasure walk down Jasmine Street!
This is الياسمين.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'she' or 'it' (feminine).

examples.trans: Take a piece of bread while it is hot.
Family is what remains.

meanings.note: Singulative noun ('one tree') of collective شجر ('trees').

examples.text: قطفنا ليمون أصفر طازة من شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: We picked fresh yellow lemons from the courtyard tree.

examples.text: ظل الشجرة بيبرد القعدة وقت الظهر.
examples.trans: The shade of the tree cools the seating area at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian possessive word ('belonging to'); agrees in gender: تبع (m.), تبعت (f.), تبعون (pl.).

examples.text: اليوم آخر يوم بأسبوع التجربة تبعك.
examples.trans: Today is the last day of your trial week.
My brother's piano teacher!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شبابيك.

examples.trans: The window overlooks the courtyard tree.
We painted the wooden shutters in summer.

meanings.note: From قوس, an arch or bow: arched windows are شبابيك مقوسة.

examples.trans: The mosque's door is arched and tall.
They have old arched windows.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غرف.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Numeral 'nine'; short form تسع (tisa') before a plural noun (تسع دقايق 'nine minutes').

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: The word 'بلكونة' (balkoonet) means 'balcony'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وشوفوا لفوق على بلكونة الساحة الخشبية بالطابق التاني—نجمة حمرا فاقعة مرسومة!
examples.trans: And look up on the second-floor wooden courtyard balcony—a bright red painted star!
This is بلكونة.

meanings.note: The word 'خشبي' (el-khashabiyye) means 'wooden'. It is a common adj in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وشوفوا لفوق على بلكونة الساحة الخشبية بالطابق التاني—نجمة حمرا فاقعة مرسومة!
examples.trans: And look up on the second-floor wooden courtyard balcony—a bright red painted star!
This is خشبي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: طوابق.

examples.trans: Your room is on the second floor on the right.
The building has three storeys.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine حمرا (hamra); شاي أحمر means black tea.

examples.trans: Would you like coffee or black tea?
There is a red ribbon on my suitcase.

meanings.note: Idiomatic Arabic colour modifier (أصفر فاقع 'bright lemon yellow', أخضر فاقع 'vivid green').

examples.text: لون الليمون الأصفر الفاقع طالع حلو جنب الأخضر.
examples.trans: The bright lemon-yellow colour looks great next to the green.

examples.text: ما بدنا لون فاقع، بدنا أخضر هادي متل الغابة.
examples.trans: We don't want a flashy shade—we want a calm forest green.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'why?'.

examples.trans: Why did the person run off without his bag?
Why do you keep looking at the clock?

meanings.note: The word 'رسام' (rassaam) means 'mapmaker'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ليش رسام الخرايط رسم نجمة حمرا على بلكونة ساحتنا اللي فوق؟!
examples.trans: Why did the mapmaker paint a red star on our upstairs courtyard balcony?!
This is رسام.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: خرايط.

examples.trans: Look at the folded map inside the box.
We drew a small map of the street.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for drawing a picture, a map or a plan.

examples.trans: He drew me a map to the shop on a piece of paper.

examples.text: بنتي بترسم بيوت وشجر كل يوم.
examples.trans: My daughter draws houses and trees every day.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نجوم.

examples.trans: The sky is clear and full of stars tonight.
The guesthouse service deserves five stars!

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Jordanian relative pronoun ('who, which, that') for any gender or number.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: The word 'بلكي' (balki) means 'perhaps'. It is a common adv in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بلكي المغلف الصغير المختوم بالشمع بجيبتك فيه الجواب يا نور!
examples.trans: Perhaps the small wax-sealed envelope in your pocket has the answer, Nour!
This is بلكي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مغلفات.

examples.trans: There is a white envelope taped to the door.
We opened the thick envelope calmly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صغيرة, plural: صغار).

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: The word 'مختوم' (el-makhtoom) means 'sealed'. It is a common adj in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: كيف رح تساعدنا ورقة فاضية نفتح المغلف الصغير المختوم؟
examples.trans: How does a blank piece of paper help us open the small sealed envelope?
This is مختوم.

meanings.note: The word 'شمع' (bish-shame3) means 'with wax'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بلكي المغلف الصغير المختوم بالشمع بجيبتك فيه الجواب يا نور!
examples.trans: Perhaps the small wax-sealed envelope in your pocket has the answer, Nour!
This is شمع.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: جيب.

examples.trans: Put the key in the coat pocket.
The paper is in my right pocket.

في.gloss: there is; there are; is there?

meanings.en: there is; there are; is there?
meanings.note: Spoken Levantine existential word ('there is / there are'); negated as ما في ('there is no / there are no').

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: The word 'جواب' (el-jawaab) means 'the answer'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بلكي المغلف الصغير المختوم بالشمع بجيبتك فيه الجواب يا نور!
examples.trans: Perhaps the small wax-sealed envelope in your pocket has the answer, Nour!
This is جواب.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Common defective verb for walking on foot or things running smoothly.

examples.text: ممنوع تمشي عكاحلك لحد بكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: You mustn't walk on your ankle until tomorrow morning.

examples.text: مشينا عالهدا بالساحة بعد ما وقفت المطر.
examples.trans: We walked gently across the courtyard after the rain stopped.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أدلة.

examples.trans: I bought the Amman travel guide.
The guesthouse is listed in the annual guide.

meanings.note: The word 'شرف' (b-sharaf) means 'honestly'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: مشينا كل دليل بشرف—حتى رامي ولفته الزايدة—فخلينا نفتحه!
examples.trans: We walked every clue honestly—even Rami and his extra circle—so let us open it!
This is شرف.

meanings.note: The word 'رامي' (رامي) means 'رامي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: سؤال حلو، لأنه رامي بيمشي كأنه عم يلحق باص رايح!
examples.trans: Good question, because Rami walks like he is chasing a departing bus!
This is رامي.

meanings.note: Versatile Jordanian noun meaning a wrapped parcel (اللفة البيضا), a pastry roll (لفة قرفة, also pl. لفائف), a street/stair turn (عاللفة), or a wrench turn (لفة، لفتين).

examples.text: أكلت لفة قرفة سخنة مع الشاي.
examples.trans: I ate a warm cinnamon roll with tea.
Watch the tight turn on the stairs.

meanings.note: The word 'زايد' (el-zaayde) means 'extra'. It is a common adj in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: مشينا كل دليل بشرف—حتى رامي ولفته الزايدة—فخلينا نفتحه!
examples.trans: We walked every clue honestly—even Rami and his extra circle—so let us open it!
This is زايد.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

إلى.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.en: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)
meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: The word 'اللقاء' (اللقاء) means 'اللقاء'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: Goodbye!
This is اللقاء.
